core.title: Define each wagon as one separable, coherent, artifact-bounded unit of a journey
core.given: A planner authors or reshapes a wagon in a journey, or composes wagons into a train.
core.when: The planner names the wagon and sets its boundary, artifacts and features.
core.then: Define the wagon as one subject/action/goal unit of the domain, separable from its siblings, that consumes and produces declared artifacts, groups the features decomposing its behavior, and composes into trains without a produce/consume cycle.
prefer: Cut the wagon from siblings along a correct boundary, judged by cross-wagon coupling.
Align subject, action and goal so the outcome is measurable.
Consume and produce declared artifacts across contracts.
Group under the wagon the features that decompose its behavior.
avoid: Wagons forming a produce/consume cycle with siblings in a train.
Describing how the wagon executes at runtime; that is a coder/tester concern.
Treating this definition as itself enforced; enforcement lives in the constraint/rule nodes that require it.
core.why: A wagon is the planner's domain-decomposition unit; a stable shared meaning lets the enforceable wagon conventions agree on what they protect.
evidence: This node is an advisory semantic anchor: it enforces nothing directly and is not bound to a validator; compliance is established transitively via planner.wagon.separability, planner.wagon.coupling-complexity, planner.wagon.semantic-coherence, planner.wagon.produce-consume-artifacts, planner.wagon.artifact-contracts, planner.wagon.no-consume-cycle and planner.wagon.features.

Reviewer confirms the wagon names one subject/action/goal with a measurable outcome, lists declared consumed/produced artifacts, groups the features decomposing its behavior, and does not close a produce/consume cycle in its train.
verification: Advisory semantic anchor with no detector of its own: this rule enforces nothing directly, is not itself bound to a validator, and must not be treated as directly enforced; it is transitively protected by the enforceable wagon conventions that require it (planner.wagon.separability, planner.wagon.coupling-complexity, planner.wagon.semantic-coherence, planner.wagon.produce-consume-artifacts, planner.wagon.artifact-contracts, planner.wagon.no-consume-cycle, planner.wagon.features).

A review of a wagon definition checks the definitional property set wagon -> {separable, semantically-coherent, artifact-producing, artifact-consuming, acyclic, feature-bearing}: separable = cut from siblings along a correct boundary; semantically-coherent = subject/action/goal align and the outcome is measurable; artifacts = consumes and produces declared artifacts across contracts; acyclic = no produce/consume cycle among wagons of a train; feature-bearing = groups the features that decompose its behavior. Each property is detailed by its corresponding enforceable convention.

Recognizing a planning artifact as a wagon or train definition has no portable observer (the file_kind activation fact is needs_new_observer): this rule mandates no path, glob or suffix and defers that classification to the realizing stack's plan-artifact profile facts (plan root, plan-artifact kinds).

fires: Planner adds a new wagon to a journey or train.
Planner splits one wagon into two or merges sibling wagons.
Planner rewrites a wagon's subject/action/goal, its measurable outcome, or its consumed/produced artifacts.
Planner adds, removes or moves features under a wagon, changing how the wagon's behavior is decomposed into features.
doesNotFire: Coder or tester work on how a wagon executes at runtime (code, handlers, tests).

Editing the wording or acceptances of a feature inside a wagon when the wagon's identity, artifacts, boundary, feature grouping, behavioral decomposition, subject/action/goal alignment and outcome measurability are all unaffected.
Planning documents that do not define or compose wagons.

neutralityNotes: The Bun rewrite of this convention is already stack-neutral: it names no runtime, framework, language, package manager, file suffix or path. Wagon/train/journey, the semantic_anchor term and the sibling convention ids (planner.wagon.*) are method-level planning vocabulary shared by every stack realization, so nothing was relegated to bunOnly and the core needs no profile data (profileRequirements is empty; no keys are missing). The one non-portable point is recognizing a planning artifact as a wagon or train definition: the file_kind activation fact is needs_new_observer, and the core keeps that deference (no mandated glob; the realizing stack classifies plan artifacts via its own plan-artifact profile facts), recorded in core.verification. activation.fires and activation.doesNotFire are carried over verbatim because they are already role-level neutral; the per-fact notes were dropped from the core facts but their substance survives in the values and in verification.
